elements.note: The service reports one period; opening and closing the datasets and reading DATEPARM stay in the step.

elements.design: ReportHeaderWriter, HeadersWriter, DetailWriter, PageTotalsWriter, AccountTotalsWriter, GrandTotalsWriter
elements.note: The design names six writers only as rule elements. Paging and totals are one stateful ReportPager; the 133-column line formats are pure functions in ReportLayout.
The step reads the one DATEPARM record and passes a Period value; the service never sees the file.

Transaction, CardXref, TransactionType and TransactionCategory are the shared domain records. ReportHeader, ReportPageTotals, ReportAccountTotals and ReportGrandTotals are not records: the totals are BigDecimal state in ReportPager and the lines are ReportLayout functions.

rules.note: A new card number closes the previous card's group and looks up its cross-reference once per group.
The end-of-input branch: the last amount is added again before the final page and grand totals (Q-02).
The grand total line is written without counting towards the page.

quirks.note: NEXT SENTENCE leaves the PERFORM loop: the first transaction processed outside the DATEPARM period ends the report with no page, account or grand totals.
verifiedBy: blank processed timestamp ends the report (Q-01)

quirks.note: At end of input the last record's amount is displayed and added to the totals a second time; the final page and grand totals follow, and the last card's account total is never written.
On INVALID KEY the program displays the FD key (not the INTO record) and abends, so the stale cross-reference is never used.
On INVALID KEY the program displays the FD key and abends; the stale type record is never used.
On INVALID KEY the program displays the FD key and abends; the stale category record is never used.

deviations.what: Six writer elements became one ReportPager (paging and totals) and ReportLayout (line formats).
A failed lookup raises MissingReference; the step displays the same INVALID ... message with the key, then abends with status 23.
deviations.behaviour: none (the abend scenarios match SYSOUT, datasets and return code)

deviations.what: DATEPARM is read by the step. With no date record the service is never called, as the COBOL sets END-OF-FILE before the loop.

smeFindings.finding: The final page total and the grand total overstate the report by the last transaction's amount, and the last card's account total line is missing. SYSOUT also carries two debug lines (TRAN-AMT, WS-PAGE-TOTAL).
smeFindings.evidence: normalizedEqualsGnuCobolOracle matches the GnuCOBOL report byte for byte, including the doubled amount; 'one transaction' shows the grand total at twice the single amount.
smeFindings.recommendation: Keep for parity. A fix (count each amount once, write the last account total, drop the debug DISPLAYs) changes TRANREPT on purpose and needs a new approved requirement and requirementsHash.

smeFindings.finding: One transaction outside the DATEPARM period silently truncates the report, with no totals. In TRANREPT the SORT INCLUDE filters by dates from in-stream SYMNAMES, while CBTRN03C reads DATEPARM, so the quirk fires whenever the two sources disagree.
smeFindings.evidence: Scenario 'period ends mid-file (Q-01 stops early)'; TRANREPT.jcl STEP05R SYMNAMES (PARM-START-DATE, PARM-END-DATE) vs STEP10R DATEPARM.
smeFindings.recommendation: Keep for parity. Operations should derive both from one source; the business decides whether out-of-period records should be skipped instead of ending the report.
